page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 64 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The dedicated CPU cores operate at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and are supported by a cache hierarchy including 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 caches. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core processing, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the lower 25th percentile, reflecting its older generation architecture. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, supported by the 64 vCPUs. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth testing in the top 25th percentile at 192.72 GB/sec, while small-block reads and large-block writes maintain average throughput. Cryptographic and vector processing are aided by hardware-level support for AES and AVX-512 instructions.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5.16xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for legacy enterprise workloads that require substantial memory and core counts without the premium cost of newer generation hardware. It is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale container orchestration where balanced CPU-to-memory ratios are required, though it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or modern LLM text generation due to its lower single-core performance.
